title: Avoidance transactions - clawing back assets before insolvency
p1: What if a company transfers away its valuable assets just before going bankrupt? Can those assets simply disappear? The answer may surprise many business owners: sometimes, the law can bring them back.
p2: A common misconception is that once an asset is sold or moved, creditors have lost their chance. In many insolvency systems, certain transactions made before failure can be reviewed and reversed. These are called avoidance transactions.
p3: The idea is simple: a business should not be allowed to unfairly move wealth away from creditors when insolvency is approaching. For example, paying one connected party unusually early or transferring assets for far less than their value may raise concerns. A court or insolvency professional may be able to recover those assets for fair distribution. The practical lesson? Actions taken before financial collapse can still have legal consequences.
conclusion: Should businesses have more responsibility for transactions made shortly before insolvency, or should owners have complete freedom to manage assets until the end?
